name: Pallanganmiddang
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Read Blake & Reid 1999 (Aboriginal History 23, ANU Press PDF): language known only from 4 old wordlists; the paper contains no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Blake, Barry J. & Julie Reid. 2002. The Dhudhuroa language of northeastern Victoria: a description based on historical sources. Aboriginal History 26: 177-210.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Has a 'Stress' paragraph (p. ~187: 'In the vast majority of Australian languages stress falls on the first syllable, but we cannot assume that this is always the case.. There is not enough information for us to be able to say much about stress'), but this concerns Dhudhuroa (dhud1236), not Pallanganmiddang; Pallanganmiddang ('Pall') appears only as a lexical-comparison label.

sources.citation: Blake, Barry J. & Julie Reid. 1998. Classifying Victorian languages. In B. J. Blake (ed.), Wathawurrung and the Colac language of southern Victoria, 1-58. Pacific Linguistics C-147. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Pallanganmiddang gets a two-line location note (p. 4) and rows in the comparative wordlist; the only stress remarks (pp. 5-6 and fn. 11) are that 'in most Australian languages the stress is on the first syllable' and that Madhi-Madhi is exceptional — nothing specific to Pallanganmiddang.

sources.citation: Curr, Edward M. 1886. The Australian Race, vol. 3. Melbourne: Government Printer. No. 213 'Upper Murray' by — Mitchell, pp. 562-563; prefatory remark p. 543.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Raw 109-word list without accent marks; Curr's prefatory remark (p. 543) only says it 'belongs to an isolated tribe on the Upper Murray, of which but three members were left'.

sources.citation: Smyth, R. Brough. 1878. The Aborigines of Victoria, vol. 2. Melbourne: Government Printer. p. 67 'Tangambalanga. Pallanganmiddah Tribe' (46 words, Thomas Mitchell).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; naming (Pallanganmiddang vs Waywurru, citing Lissarrague & Wafer 2008: 65) and classification only; cites Clark 2005, Walsh 1981, Tryon 2007, Blake & Reid 1999.

sources.citation: Blake, Barry J. & Julie Reid. 1999. Pallanganmiddang: a language of the Upper Murray. Aboriginal History 23: 15-31.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The Phonology section (pp. 17-20) covers consonant inventory, final consonants, clusters, vowels and vowel length in monosyllables (mii 'eye', ngaa 'nose'); a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence/intonation returns no hits. The paper states the language is known only from four old wordlists (Mitchell in Smyth 1878, Mitchell in Curr 1886, Robinson ms, Murdock 1900) and 'There is no grammatical information available on Pallanganmiddang' (p. 20).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page pall1243; Wikipedia 'Pallanganmiddang language'.
sources.note: Glottolog lists only overview-type references (no descriptive grammar/phonology; Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology). Wikipedia's phonology summary is drawn from Blake & Reid 1999 and contains no stress information.
